key_insight: Dead-end pores are not just inactive voids: when they are densely distributed along flow paths, they can increase intrinsic permeability through local hydrodynamic interactions at junctions.
engineering_relevance: Permeability predictions for porous materials should account for the spatial organization of dead-end pores, not only porosity and pore-size statistics.
method: Performed pore-scale flow simulations on multiple pore architectures.
Compared heterogeneous dead-end pore arrangements, controlled granular assemblies, and a minimal single-channel model.
Varied dead-end pore density, depth, and junction orientation while keeping the transmitting network fixed.
evidence_signal: The simulations show that permeability increases with dead-end pore density along percolating paths, while pore depth and orientation have negligible effect.
watch_item: The proposed relationship is based on idealized pore-scale geometries, so transfer to real rocks or packed media may require calibration.
paper_title: Pore-shape and its spatial organization control intrinsic permeability of porous media
